20261118-physics-g03.goal: Apply the principles of Light and shadow to solve the reasoning problem.
20261118-physics-g03.material: [E3 Physics Inquiry] Problem wey dey apply the principles of Light and shadow. On flat ground wey no get friction, force $F = 10\text{ N}$ push object of mass $m = 2\text{ kg}$ reach distance $4\text{ m}$. Which statement describe the work $W$ and acceleration $a$ correctly?
20261118-physics-g03.s.s1.prompt: [E3 Physics Inquiry] Problem wey dey apply the principles of Light and shadow. On flat ground wey no get friction, force $F = 10\text{ N}$ push object of mass $m = 2\text{ kg}$ reach distance $4\text{ m}$. Which statement describe the work $W$ and acceleration $a$ correctly?
20261118-physics-g03.s.s1.explain:
Step 1: From Newton second law $F = ma$, acceleration $a = \frac{F}{m} = \frac{10\text{ N}}{2\text{ kg}} = 5\text{ m/s}^2$.
Step 2: Work wey dem do na $W = F \cdot s = 10\text{ N} \times 4\text{ m} = 40\text{ J}$.
Step 3: So acceleration na $5\text{ m/s}^2$ and work na $40\text{ J}$.

20261118-physics-g03.s.s1.hint.1: Definition of work: use formula $W = F \times s$.

20261121-physics-g03-1.title: Light and shadow
20261121-physics-g03-1.goal: Apply the principles of Light and shadow to solve the reasoning problem.
20261121-physics-g03-1.material: [E3 Physics Inquiry (Advanced)] Free fall analysis related to Light and shadow. Object fall from rest for vacuum under gravity $g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$. Wetin be the velocity $v$ and distance $h$ after $t = 3\text{ s}$?
20261121-physics-g03-1.s.s1.prompt: [E3 Physics Inquiry (Advanced)] Free fall analysis related to Light and shadow. Object fall from rest for vacuum under gravity $g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$. Wetin be the velocity $v$ and distance $h$ after $t = 3\text{ s}$?
20261121-physics-g03-1.s.s1.explain:
Step 1: Velocity $v = gt = 9.8 \times 3 = 29.4\text{ m/s}$.
Step 2: Distance $h = \frac{1}{2}gt^2 = 0.5 \times 9.8 \times 9 = 44.1\text{ m}$.
Step 3: So $v = 29.4\text{ m/s}$ and $h = 44.1\text{ m}$.

Step 1: Velocity $v = gt = 9.8 \times 3 = 29.4\text{ m/s}$.
Step 2: Distance $h = \frac{1}{2}gt^2 = 0.5 \times 9.8 \times 9 = 44.1\text{ m}$.
Step 3: So $v = 29.4\text{ m/s}$ and $h = 44.1\text{ m}$.

20261122-physics-g04-1.material: [E4 Physics Inquiry] Problem wey dey apply the principles of Balancing and lever. On flat ground wey no get friction, force $F = 10\text{ N}$ push object of mass $m = 2\text{ kg}$ reach distance $4\text{ m}$. Which statement describe the work $W$ and acceleration $a$ correctly?
20261122-physics-g04-1.s.s1.prompt: [E4 Physics Inquiry] Problem wey dey apply the principles of Balancing and lever. On flat ground wey no get friction, force $F = 10\text{ N}$ push object of mass $m = 2\text{ kg}$ reach distance $4\text{ m}$. Which statement describe the work $W$ and acceleration $a$ correctly?
20261122-physics-g04-1.s.s1.explain:
Step 1: From Newton second law $F = ma$, acceleration $a = \frac{F}{m} = \frac{10\text{ N}}{2\text{ kg}} = 5\text{ m/s}^2$.
Step 2: Work wey dem do na $W = F \cdot s = 10\text{ N} \times 4\text{ m} = 40\text{ J}$.
Step 3: So acceleration na $5\text{ m/s}^2$ and work na $40\text{ J}$.
